 ATP Stockholm Semifinal Predictions Including Taylor Fritz vs Lorenzo Musetti 
 Share Share this article
 × X Facebook LinkedIn WhatsApp Reddit Email Copy 
 The indoor hard courts at ATP Stockholm are set for two intriguing semifinal encounters, with three seeded players and an unexpected challenger battling for a place in the final. Taylor Fritz and Lorenzo Musetti renew their rivalry, while Alejandro Tabilo faces Thiago Agustin Tirante in a matchup that promises a compelling contrast in experience and style. As always, we at LWOT will offer our predictions for every match on the schedule. But who will advance ?
 ATP Stockholm Semifinal Predictions
 Alejandro Tabilo vs Thiago Agustin Tirante
 Head-to-Head: Tabilo 4–1 Tirante
 Alejandro Tabilo has a chance to reach another ATP final after an encouraging run at ATP Stockholm. The Chilean overcame Lorenzo Sonego in a demanding three-set encounter before producing an impressive straight-sets win over sixth seed Alex Michelsen, 7-5 7-6. His performance against Michelsen was particularly encouraging, as he saved six of the seven break points he faced and showed greater composure in the important moments.
 Tabilo’s experience at this level gives him an advantage heading into the semifinal. Ranked inside the world’s top 35, he has established himself as a dangerous opponent across surfaces, although indoor hard courts are not traditionally where his game has been most effective. Reaching his first indoor hard-court semifinal is another encouraging development, particularly after a difficult stretch of results before arriving in Sweden.
 Tirante, however, should not be underestimated. The Argentine has enjoyed an equally productive week, defeating Jaume Munar in straight sets before overcoming Aleksandr Shevchenko 7-6 6-7  6-3 in a lengthy quarterfinal. He also received a walkover against Tomas Martin Etcheverry in the second round, giving him a little more recovery time heading into this ATP Stockholm semifinal encounter.
 The head-to-head record favours Tabilo 4-1, although there is an important detail worth considering. Tirante won their only previous hard-court meeting, at the 2025 Cancun Challenger, taking it in straight sets. The Chilean has since won their three subsequent encounters, including two meetings in 2026, but this will be their first meeting on an indoor hard court.
 Tirante possesses an effective first serve and can take time away from his opponent when he finds his rhythm. However, Tabilo’s greater experience at ATP Tour level, consistency from the baseline and ability to construct points patiently could prove decisive. The Chilean has also shown encouraging composure during the important moments this week, something that should serve him well in a potentially tight semifinal.
 Tirante has the tools to make this competitive, but Tabilo’s experience and superior record in their rivalry make him the more convincing choice. Expect the Chilean to navigate a difficult opening set before gradually establishing control at ATP Stockholm.
 Prediction: Tabilo in 3 
 Taylor Fritz vs Lorenzo Musetti
 Head-to-Head: Musetti 5–3 Fritz
 Taylor Fritz and Lorenzo Musetti renew their rivalry in what promises to be one of the most compelling matches of the ATP Stockholm semifinals. The pair have faced each other eight times, with Musetti holding a 5-3 advantage. The Italian also won their most recent encounter, defeating Fritz 6-3 6-4 in the Lyon final just a couple of weeks ago.
 Musetti has been particularly impressive on indoor hard courts this season, compiling a 10-2 record on the surface. His Lyon title was another demonstration of his ability to adapt his game to quicker conditions, while his victory over Alexander Zverev at the Paris Masters further underlined his growing confidence. He has carried that form into ATP Stockholm, defeating Toby Samuel and Ugo Humbert to reach the last four.
 His quarterfinal against Humbert was particularly demanding. Musetti recovered from losing the second set and falling behind early in the decider to secure a 7-6(5), 3-6, 6-4 victory after two hours and 29 minutes. His ability to regain control under pressure will be important against an opponent who thrives on aggressive baseline exchanges.
 Fritz, meanwhile, has had a relatively straightforward route to the semifinals. The American opened his campaign with a first-round bye before defeating Cameron Norrie 7-5 6-3. He subsequently advanced through a walkover after Holger Rune withdrew from their quarterfinal with a minor hamstring injury.
 The world No. 10 is reaching his seventh semifinal of the season and his third in four weeks. He is also chasing another year-end top-10 finish , with one more victory at ATP Stockholm enough to secure that achievement. His powerful serve, ability to dictate from the baseline and experience on indoor hard courts make him a formidable opponent for Musetti.
 Importantly, Fritz has won two of their three previous indoor hard-court encounters. That statistic offers encouragement despite Musetti’s overall advantage in their rivalry. The American’s first-strike tennis is particularly effective in these conditions, where shorter rallies and aggressive serving can limit the Italian’s opportunities to use his variety.
 Musetti’s recent victory in Lyon gives him a psychological advantage, but Fritz has the weapons to make this a very different contest. The American has also benefited from additional recovery time after his quarterfinal walkover, although the lack of match practice could be a factor if Musetti starts aggressively.
 Ultimately, Musetti’s excellent indoor record and greater variety make him a difficult opponent, but Fritz’s serving advantage and stronger record in their indoor meetings give him a slight edge. I expect the Italian to make him work for it, particularly if he can extend the rallies and prevent Fritz from dictating with his forehand.
 Prediction: Fritz in 3
